description: Composite EBSD figure of the initial microstructure of a TiB2-reinforced Al-added steel, mixing pseudo-3D stereographic maps, 2D orientation maps and histograms. (a), (a1), (a2) are pseudo-3D cubes with 50 μm scale bars: IPF colouring with an IPF key (0001, 12-10, 001 / 01-10, 101, 111) and RD/TD/ND axes; the phase map with legend γ (blue), δ-F (red), TiB2 (yellow); and the KAM map with a low→high colour scale. (b), (b1), (b2) are the matching 2D IPF, phase and KAM maps (20 μm scale bars, (b2) marked TD/RD). The phase maps show alternating red δ-ferrite and blue austenite lamellae with elongated yellow TiB2 particles. (b3) plots grain-size histograms (x = Grain size (μm), 0–18; y = Relative frequency (%), 0–25) for Austenite_avg = 3.9 μm (blue) and δ-Ferrite_avg = 4.4 μm (red), with a δ-ferrite inset. (c), (c1), (c2) are GOS maps accompanied by Min/Max/Fraction tables; (c3) plots GOS frequency (x = Grain orientation spread (°), 0–10; y = Relative frequency (%), 0–70) with Austenite_avg (<2° 90.8%) and δ-Ferrite_avg (<2° 52.2%). The figure demonstrates a banded γ + δ-ferrite matrix with dispersed TiB2 in which austenite is largely recrystallized while δ-ferrite retains high GOS.

subfigures.description: Pseudo-3D stereographic IPF map cube with RD/TD/ND axes, IPF colour key (0001, 12-10, 001, 01-10, 101, 111) and a 50 μm scale bar; grains rendered in multiple colours.
Pseudo-3D phase-map cube with legend γ (blue), δ-F (red), TiB2 (yellow) and a 50 μm scale bar; alternating red δ-ferrite and blue austenite bands with elongated yellow TiB2 particles.
Pseudo-3D KAM map cube with a blue→red low→high colour scale bar and 50 μm scale bar; green high-misorientation regions within a blue matrix.
2D IPF map (labelled IPF) with the same IPF colour key and a 20 μm scale bar; equiaxed multi-coloured grains.
2D phase map with legend γ (blue), δ-F (red), TiB2 (yellow) and 20 μm scale bar; clearly banded red/blue lamellae with elongated yellow particles.
2D KAM map with TD/RD arrows, low→high colour bar and 20 μm scale bar; green (higher KAM) regions preferentially located in the ferrite lamellae.

Grain-size histogram: x = Grain size (μm) 0–18, y = Relative frequency (%) 0–25; blue bars Austenite_avg = 3.9 μm, red bars δ-Ferrite_avg = 4.4 μm; inset shows the δ-ferrite distribution peaked near 2 μm.

2D GOS map (labelled GOS) over the whole microstructure, mostly blue with red/yellow patches in bands; accompanying table Min/Max/Fraction rows 0–2: 0.826, 2–3: 0.050, 3–4: 0.036, 4–5: 0.035, 5–12: 0.051.
2D γ-GOS map (austenite only) dominated by blue; table rows 0–2: 0.908, 2–3: 0.030, 3–4: 0.028, 4–5: 0.022, 5–12: 0.012.
2D δ-F-GOS map (δ-ferrite only) with much larger red/orange fraction; table rows 0–2: 0.522, 2–3: 0.120, 3–4: 0.081, 4–5: 0.096, 5–12: 0.180; 20 μm scale bar.

GOS frequency histogram: x = Grain orientation spread (°) 0–10, y = Relative frequency (%) 0–70; blue Austenite_avg (<2° 90.8%) strongly peaked at low GOS, red δ-Ferrite_avg (<2° 52.2%); inset shows the δ-ferrite distribution with a secondary high-GOS peak near 8.5°.

observations.observation: The phase-map legend encodes γ (austenite) as blue, δ-F (δ-ferrite) as red and TiB2 as yellow.
Phase maps (a1, b1) show a banded/layered structure of alternating red δ-ferrite and blue austenite lamellae, with elongated yellow TiB2 particles aligned with the bands.
The IPF colour key of (a) and (b) is labelled 0001, 12-10, 001 and 01-10, 101, 111, with RD/TD/ND direction axes marked on (a) and TD/RD arrows on (b2).
KAM maps (a2, b2) use a low→high colour bar (blue = low, red = high) and show higher-KAM (green) regions concentrated in the ferrite lamellae, while most austenite appears blue.
The 2D maps (b, b1, b2, c, c1, c2) carry 20 μm scale bars, whereas the pseudo-3D cubes (a, a1, a2) carry 50 μm scale bars.
Panel (b3) prints Austenite_avg = 3.9 μm and δ-Ferrite_avg = 4.4 μm in its legend, with grain size plotted to 18 μm and relative frequency to 25%.
Panel (c3) prints Austenite_avg (<2° 90.8%) and δ-Ferrite_avg (<2° 52.2%), with grain orientation spread plotted from 0 to 10° and relative frequency from 0 to 70%.
The GOS fraction tables print the 0–2° fraction as 0.826 for the whole map (c), 0.908 for γ-GOS (c1) and 0.522 for δ-F-GOS (c2), and the 5–12° fraction as 0.051, 0.012 and 0.180 respectively.

The caption states that area fractions of austenite, ferrite and TiB2 estimated from EBSD are about 59%, 28% and 13% respectively, and that the figure shows the initial microstructure of the present steel.
The caption states that TD and RD refer to the transverse direction and rolling direction respectively, and that separate colour keys are provided for the IPF, phase, KAM and GOS maps.
The citing text states the average ferrite band thickness is 4.3 μm versus 12.1 μm for austenite layers, and that δ-ferrite grains are elongated parallel to the rolling direction.

The citing text states austenite grains with GOS < 2° are considered fully recrystallized and account for 90.8% (area fraction) of austenite, whereas recrystallized δ-ferrite accounts for only 52.2% of the ferrite phase.
The citing text states δ-ferrite grains have an average size of 4.4 μm while austenite grains are mostly equiaxed with an average size of ~3.9 μm.
The citing text attributes the higher KAM values in ferrite lamellae to a non-uniform strain distribution, with no evident misorientation accumulation in most austenite grains.

measured_quantities: kernel average misorientation (KAM, colour scale only, no printed unit)
unreadable_items: Panel (a): the small IPF colour-key labels inside the cube are only partially legible; the identical key in (b) was used to read them
Panels (c), (c1), (c2): the Min/Max/Fraction tables are legible, but the exact colour swatch assigned to each range is inferred by position rather than by printed text
